name: module_start
notes: exports: 0x0_935CD196. init chain: sds_init_args(arglen) 0x81003b64, 0x81001d24, sds_parttab_init, sds_handle_heap_init, 0x81003a74, 0x81005004; any failure -> 2 (SCE_KERNEL_START_FAILED), else 0

name: sds_handle_heap_init
notes: heap "SceSdStorDeviceHandle" of 0x2000 bytes (opt {0x1c, 1}) -> 0x81007038; returns the error if negative

name: sds_handle_open
notes: allocates a 0x58-byte handle from the handle heap (NULL -> 0x8001000C), fast mutex "SceSdStorDeviceHandle"; under the device mutex (p->dev+8... p[2]) copies sector size (dev+0x40), start sector (p[0]), sector count (p[1]) and device (dev+0x44 -> +0x54); flags at +0x4c (1 read, 2 write), partition at +0x50; increments the open count of the device class (0x81007020[sds_dev_class(dev)])

name: sds_handle_close
notes: finalises the handle mutex (error -> return), decrements the class open count, clears the fields and frees the handle

name: sds_handle_read
prototype: int sds_handle_read(sds_handle *h, ?, u64 offset, void *buf, u32 len)
notes: needs open flag 1 (else 0x8001000D); offset and len must be multiples of the sector size (else 0x80010022) and inside the partition (sector count * sector size; else 0x80010021). Reads in chunks of at most 0x2000000 - sector bytes via sds_dev_read(dev, buf, start + offset/sector, count); an error after some data returns the bytes done, else the error; returns len on success

name: sds_handle_write
prototype: int sds_handle_write(sds_handle *h, ?, u64 offset, const void *buf, u32 len)
notes: write twin of sds_handle_read: open flag 2, same alignment/range checks, sds_dev_write (0x81002c58) in chunks of at most 0x2000000 - sector bytes

name: sds_part_set_entire
prototype: void sds_part_set_entire(int devno, sds_dev *d, u32 nsectors, const void *id6)
notes: fills the "entire device" partition slot (+0x218): start 0, size nsectors, owner d, name "%01d%02d" (devno, 16) at +0x228, 6 id bytes at +0x22c

name: sds_parse_sce_mbr
notes: the device sector-0 buffer (d+0x54) must start with "Sony Computer Entertainment Inc." (32 bytes) and end with 0xAA55, else 0x8001002F (not a Sony MBR). 16 entries of 17 bytes from +0x50: an entry with a nonzero byte at +8 (partition code) becomes slot i at d+0x58+i*0x1c {start sector (+0), sector count (+4), owner, raw entry, name "%01d%02d" (devno, i), 6 bytes from entry+0xb}; empty entries are zeroed. Clears d+0x236

name: sds_parttab_init
notes: for the 5 device slots (0x81007a40, 0x238 each, sector-0 buffers 0x200 each at 0x81007040): fast mutex "SceSdStorPartitionTable", state bytes 0, buffer pointer, partition area (+0x58, 0x1dc bytes) zeroed

name: sds_dev_reset
notes: devno < 5; under the slot mutex, if state (+0x234) is nonzero: state and +0x236 := 0, +0x44..0x53 zeroed, buffer pointer restored, partition area zeroed

name: sds_dev_suspend_a
notes: under the slot mutex: saved state (+0x235) := state, state := 2

name: sds_dev_clear
notes: as sds_dev_reset (same field reset when state != 0); returns 0

name: sds_dev_suspend_b
notes: identical to sds_dev_suspend_a (separate copy): state saved to +0x235, state := 2

name: sds_dev_resume
notes: state := saved state (+0x235)

name: sds_sd_mbr_valid
notes: checks a removable card MBR against the SD Association file system rules; 0 if it conforms, else 0x8001002F. Partition entries 2-4 must be all zero and the signature 0xAA55; entry 1 boot flag 0 or 0x80. Its system ID must match the card size in sectors: < 0x7FA8 FAT12 (1), < 0x10000 FAT16 (4), < 0x400000 FAT16 (6), < 0x4000000 (32 GiB) FAT32 (0x0B, or 0x0C when the end LBA is past 0xFB0400), larger exFAT (7). The start and end CHS must equal the values computed with the SD-spec heads/sectors table for that size (or FE FF FF past 0xFB0400 sectors). The partition must lie inside the card, and for cards of 0x400000 sectors and up its start must be a multiple of the boundary unit (0x80, 0x2000, 0x8000, 0x10000 or 0x20000 sectors by size). So an MBR with any other type, NTFS on a small card for instance, does not validate

name: sds_parse_plain_mbr
prototype: int sds_parse_plain_mbr(int devno, sds_dev *d, u8 *card, int kind)
notes: kind 1 (SD card): ksceSdifGetSdContextPartValidateSd(card[0]) (NULL -> 0x80010013), card size = ctx+0x90 >> 9, and the MBR must pass sds_sd_mbr_valid. Other kinds: sector 0 must end in 0xAA55 and must not look like a boot sector (EB xx 90 or E9). If accepted, MBR partition 1 becomes slot 0 (start, size from +0x1C6/+0x1CA, raw entry, name "%01d%02d" (devno, 0), id 6 bytes 01 00 01 02 01 00 from 0x810061de), slots 1-15 cleared, d+0x236 = 1. Otherwise returns 0 with no partitions (only the entire device). Only partition 1 is ever used

name: sds_sd_write_mbr
notes: formats the partition table of an SD card the SD-spec way: device (sds_dev_by_no, NULL -> 0x80010013) and SD context (NULL -> 0x80010013), size = ctx+0x90 >> 9. Builds a zeroed sector with 0xAA55 and one partition. For cards of 0x400000 sectors and up the start is the boundary unit (0x80, 0x2000, 0x8000, 0x10000, 0x20000). Smaller cards use cluster size 0x10..0x80 sectors and sectors per FAT computed for FAT12 (< 0x20000) or FAT16, with the start searched so the data area lands on a cluster boundary (start = unit - 0x21 - FAT sectors). Then the size, CHS start/end from the SD geometry table and the system ID (1/4/6/0x0B/0x0C/7 as in sds_sd_mbr_valid) are filled in. Then 0x81001e50 (must return 0), sds_dev_write(dev, sector, 0, 1) and 0x81002240(dev) to re-scan

name: sds_is_sce_mbr
notes: 0 if s0 starts with "Sony Computer Entertainment Inc." and ends with 0xAA55, else 0x8001002F

name: sds_dev_scan
notes: loads the partition table of device devno once. Under the slot mutex: state 2 (suspended or removed) -> 0x80010013, state 1 (already scanned) -> 0. Else the device (sds_dev_by_no, NULL -> 0x80010013) must be ready (sds_dev_check 0x81001e50). Sector 0 goes into the slot buffer (sds_dev_read), and sds_dev_get_size (0x81002fcc) gives the size into slot+0x40/+0x48 (twice). Then state := 1, +0x236 := 0. Per device: dev 0 (internal eMMC): the "entire" slot (code 0x4F, id 4f 0f ..), then the Sony MBR is required (else 0x8001002F) and its 16 entries are parsed inline. dev 1: when SceSysrootForDriver_F804F761() is 0 (game-card slot) a Sony MBR is parsed if present, and with no usable partition and ksceSysrootUseExternalStorage the SD-style plain MBR (sds_parse_plain_mbr kind 0) is used instead. When F804F761 is nonzero it is an SD slot: "entire" plus partition 1 if the MBR passes sds_sd_mbr_valid. dev 2 (memory card): "entire" plus Sony MBR entries if present. dev 3 (USB mass): "entire" and plain MBR partition 1 (sds_parse_plain_mbr). dev 4: like the SD-slot case. The "entire" names are "%01d16"

name: sds_find_part
notes: resolves a device name to a partition slot (NULL if none). A 3-digit name NNN: device N/100 (< 5), slot N%100 (<= 16), after sds_dev_scan; the slot must exist and its name must match. Otherwise sds_parse_name gives {device, lp/pp, code, active}. Device 0xFF (xmc) means the default memory device: DAT_81007000 or DAT_81007001 by UseExternal/InternalStorage, else the first ready device in {2, 5} or, with ksceKernelSysrootCheckModelCapability(0xB), {2, 4, 5}; none -> 2. code 8 (userext) on device 4 or 1 is turned into pp partition 0. After sds_dev_scan, for a Sony-MBR device: pp N -> slot N (not 17), lp entire (0xF) -> slot 16, else the first slot whose raw partition code maps (sds_part_code) to code and whose active byte (+10) equals the requested one (2 = ign = any). For a plain-MBR device (+0x236 == 1) only pp N or entire

name: sds_default_ext_dev
notes: the memory-card-class device to use: hint 0, 3 or (1 with F804F761 == 0) are ignored; another hint is atomically stored in DAT_81007001 if it was unset (5). Then: internal storage only -> 0; DAT_81007001 if set; else the first ready device in the probe order {2, 5} (or {2, 4, 5} with model capability 0xB); none -> 2

name: sds_default_ext_release
notes: clears DAT_81007001 back to 5 if it holds dev (same exclusions as sds_default_ext_dev); returns the previous value or 0

name: sds_default_ext_get
notes: same selection as sds_default_ext_dev without storing a hint

name: sds_default_int_dev
notes: as sds_default_ext_dev for DAT_81007000, without the internal-storage shortcut

name: sds_default_int_release
notes: clears DAT_81007000 back to 5 if it holds dev

name: sds_default_int_get
notes: DAT_81007000, or the first ready device in the probe order, or 2

name: sds_parse_name
prototype: int sds_parse_name(const char *name, u32 len, u8 out[4])
notes: parses <dev>-<lp|pp>-<ina|act|ign>-<code> (len <= 0x14, else or on any mismatch 0x80010013): dev from {int-, ext-, gcd-, mcd-, uma-, usd-, xmc-} mapped through 0x81006280 to device {0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 0xFF}; out[1] = 0 lp / 1 pp; out[3] = 0 ina / 1 act / 2 ign; out[2] = code index in {unused, idstor, sloader, os, vsh, vshdata, vtrm, user, userext, gamero, gamerw, updater, sysdata, mediaid, pidata, entire} (0..15). For pp the code field may instead be one letter a..p giving the physical partition index. A prefix match of a field must end in "-" or be the whole remaining name

name: sds_part_code
notes: raw Sony partition code -> name index: 0..14 unchanged, 0xFF -> 15 (entire), anything else -> 0

name: sds_nop
notes: empty; called on the parsed name in sds_find_part

name: sds_dev_init
notes: for the 5 devices (0x81008558, 0x54 bytes each): fast mutex "SceSdStorDevice", +0x40 kind from 0x810063d8 {0, 1, 0xFF, 0xFF, 3}, +0x41 bus from 0x810063d0 {0, 0, 2, 3, 1}, the rest zeroed. After a BSOD reboot it powers off the SD slot (kind 1: ScePervasiveForDriver_5E20D7D5 + ksceSysconCtrlSdPower(0)) and the memory card (bus 2: ksceSysconCtrlRMRPower(0))

name: sds_dev_power_off
notes: kind 1: ScePervasiveForDriver_5E20D7D5, SD power off; bus 2: RMR (memory card) power off; returns the last error

name: sds_dev_by_no
notes: &devices[devno] for devno < 5, else NULL

name: sds_dev_index
notes: device pointer -> 0..4, else -1

name: sds_dev_check
notes: brings the device up if needed, under its mutex. State +0x42: 1 ready -> 0; 2 removed -> 0x80010013. kind 1 (game-card slot) needs ksceSdifGetCardInsertState1() == 1, then SD power on and ScePervasiveForDriver_E6728E30. It tries ksceSdifInitializeMmcDevice(1) (a game card is MMC: bus 0, then ksceSblGcAuthMgrGcAuthCartAuthentication(1)). If that fails and UseExternalStorage or SceSysrootForDriver_F804F761 is set, it tries ksceSdifInitializeSdDevice(1) up to twice (an SD card in that slot: bus 1). kind 0 (internal eMMC): InitializeMmcDevice(0) with one retry unless 0x8032001A. bus 2 (memory card): kscePervasiveRemovableMemoryGetCardInsertState != 0, RMR power on, SceMsifForDriver_4EA579EF + ksceMsifGetMsInfo up to twice. bus 3 (USB mass): only when DAT_81007004 is set (else 0x80010013); SceUsbMassForDriver_D989A9F6 gives sectors, sector size and write-protect. A device of 2^32 sectors or more (512-byte sectors: 2 TiB) is refused with 0x80024902. kind 3 (dev 4): ksceSdifGetCardInsertState2() == 1, InitializeSdDevice(3). On success: state 1, +0x44 sector size, +0x48 sector count (capacity / sector size), +0x4c (MMC ctx+0x394 / SD ctx+0xB4 / MS info), +0x50 controller context, +0x43 write-protect. Any failure powers the slot back off and leaves state 0

name: sds_dev_forget
notes: under the mutex: state 0 and the geometry/context fields cleared (no power change)

name: sds_dev_shutdown
notes: under the mutex: state 0, then SD power off for kind 1 and RMR power off for bus 2

name: sds_dev_reinit
notes: clears the geometry like sds_dev_forget, then runs the same bring-up as sds_dev_check (inlined copy; identical slot handling and errors)

name: sds_dev_mark_removed
notes: under the mutex: state 2 (removed) and the slot powered off (SD power for kind 1, RMR power for bus 2)

name: sds_dev_reinit_removable
notes: kind 0 (internal eMMC) -> 0 untouched; otherwise identical to sds_dev_reinit (inlined copy)

name: sds_dev_read
prototype: int sds_dev_read(sds_dev *d, void *buf, u32 sector, u16 count)
notes: under the device mutex, state must be 1 (else 0x80010013). bus 0 MMC: ksceSdifReadSectorMmc(ctx, sector, buf, count); bus 1 SD: ksceSdifReadSectorSd, and on 0x80320022 the card is re-initialised (InitializeSdDevice, twice unless 0x8032001A) but the error is still returned; bus 2: ksceMsifReadSector; bus 3: SceUsbMassForDriver_B80D1DF8 if registered (DAT_81007008, else 0x80010013); other -> 0x80010006. For the game-card slot (kind 1) and the memory card it brackets the transfer with SceSysrootForDriver_9BF782CA(slot, 2, pattern) - an activity indicator hook (patterns 0x810063bc on / 0x810063a8 off)

name: sds_dev_write
prototype: int sds_dev_write(sds_dev *d, const void *buf, u32 sector, u16 count)
notes: write twin of sds_dev_read: ksceSdifWriteSectorMmc / ksceSdifWriteSectorSd (same 0x80320022 re-init) / ksceMsifWriteSector / SceUsbMassForDriver_081CA197 (DAT_8100700c); indicator pattern 0x810063e0 after. Write protection (+0x43) is not checked here

name: sds_dev_media_op
notes: state 1 required (0x80010013). Game-card MMC (bus 0, kind 1): SceSdifForDriver_6CC8E28D(); internal eMMC: 0x80010010; memory card (bus 2): SceMsifForDriver_F997286B(); others 0x80010030

name: sds_dev_mmc_query
prototype: int sds_dev_mmc_query(sds_dev *d, u32 a, u32 b, u8 *out)
notes: state 1 required (0x80010013). bus 0: SceSdifForDriver_995748EA(ctx, a, b, &v); bus 1: SceSdifForDriver_E091BA2E(ctx, a, b, &v); on success *out = (u8)v. Memory card and USB: *out = 0, 0. Other -> 0x80010013

name: sds_dev_ms_op
notes: memory card only (state 1, bus 2): SceMsifForDriver_6EDE7DBA(); otherwise 0x80010013

name: sds_dev_sd_op
notes: state 1 and bus 1 (SD) required (0x80010013); kind 1 or 3 -> SceSdifForDriver_35BA9DF8(kind, a, ?, 1); other kinds 0x80010016

name: sds_dev_check_writable
notes: state 1 required (0x80010013); write-protected (+0x43 & 1) -> 0x8001000D, else 0

name: sds_dev_get_geometry
notes: state 1 required (0x80010013); out = {sector size (+0x44), sector count (+0x48), +0x4c}

name: sds_vfs_init
notes: VFS op slot 8 (init): 0

name: sds_vfs_mount
notes: VFS op slot 0: mnt+0xc0 := 0x200, mnt+0x68 := 0x14, mnt+0x44 := DAT_8100871c (the root vnode created at startup); 0

name: sds_vfs_umount
notes: VFS op slot 1: always 0x80010010 (busy) - sdstor0: can never be unmounted

name: sds_vfs_set_root
notes: VFS op slot 2: root vnode (a[2]): mnt := a[0], node_data := 0, type 1 (+0x74), +0x78 := 0x10020, size 0, +0x88 := 0

name: sds_vop_sync
notes: vop slot 23 (sync): 0

name: sds_vop_inactive
notes: vop slot 20 (inactive): 0

name: sds_vop_pwrite
notes: vop slot 19: vnode node_data (+0x48, the open handle) required (0x80010013); under the handle mutex the handle flags are temporarily replaced by the file open flags (file+4) and sds_handle_write(handle, offset, buf, len) runs

name: sds_vop_lseek
notes: vop slot 6: node_data required (0x80010013); the offset must be a multiple of the sector size (else 0x80010022); whence 0 set, 1 current (file+8), 2 end (sector count * sector size); other -> 0x80010016; a result past the end -> 0x80010021; a negative result is returned unchanged without moving. Stores the position in file+8

name: sds_vop_write
notes: vop slot 5: as sds_vop_pwrite at the file position (file+8), which advances by the bytes written

name: sds_vop_pread
notes: vop slot 18: sds_handle_read at the given offset, file open flags substituted for the handle flags

name: sds_vop_read
notes: vop slot 4: sds_handle_read at file+8, advancing it

name: sds_vop_remove
notes: vop slot 8 (remove): frees the vnode node_data (a[1]+0x48) from the mount heap (mnt+0x6c) and clears it; if the node points at a partition whose device slot is not suspended (state != 2), that 0x1C-byte partition slot is zeroed first. node_data NULL -> 0x80010013

name: sds_vop_lookup
notes: vop slot 3: allocates a 12-byte node {partition, device, 0} from the mount heap (NULL -> 0x8001000C). sds_find_part(name, len) must give a partition whose device slot exists and is not suspended (else 0x80010013, node freed). vfsGetNewVnode + vfsLockVnode; vnode+0xd0 = device class word from 0x81006428 {0x100, 0x201, 0x202, 0x203, 0x202} by device index, mount, size = partition sectors * sector size, parent, node_data, type 1, mode 0x2000 (regular file), acl_data (+0x88, 6 bytes) = the partition's 6 id bytes - these are the SceSblACMgr type-8 access rights of the partition

name: sds_vop_close
notes: vop slot 2: sds_handle_close(file->fd)

name: sds_vop_open
notes: vop slot 0: node_data and its device slot required (0x80010013); flags & 3 must be nonzero, and write on a write-protected device (sds_dev_check_writable 0x8001000D) is refused with 0x8001000D. A suspended device slot -> 0x80010013. Then SceSblACMgrForDriver_BE5667C5 (acm_check_access)(0 = current process, {type 8, &id6, 6}, 1 for read-only or 3 for read/write) - the type-8 per-program-class rights stored in the Sony partition entry. Finally sds_handle_open(partition, flags) -> file->fd (+0x20)

name: sds_vfs_decode_path_elem
notes: VFS op slot 12: a name longer than 3 characters that resolves (sds_find_part) to a partition on a device that is not suspended is rewritten to its 3-digit canonical name ("NNN", device*100 + slot), length 3; anything else is copied unchanged. So iofilemgr caches sdstor0:int-lp-act-os and sdstor0:000-style names as the same vnode

name: sds_vfs_devctl
notes: VFS op slot 11. Every command except 1 needs SceSblACMgr type-8 rights 4 from the fixed 6 bytes ff 0f 00 00 00 00 (0x8100621a), i.e. a 0x28... system program (else 0x800F090D). Names are <= 0x14 chars, parsed with sds_parse_name; xmc (0xFF) means the current default device. cmd 1 (in = partition name, out 0x10 bytes): ACMgr check with the partition's own rights; out = {start sector, sector count, controller ctx, byte from sds_dev_mmc_query, default device, 0, 0}. cmd 2: memory card only (device 2), sds_dev_ms_op. cmd 3: per device, sets the "busy/ignore" bit (sds_slot_set_flag 0x81005398) of device 2, 4 and, on an SD slot, 1. cmd 4: sds_slot_signal_insert (event bit 2), cmd 5: sds_slot_signal_remove (bit 0x10), devices 1, 2, 4 only. cmd 6 (in = {PUID, name}): device 1 (SD slot) or 4 with nothing open on it (else 0x80010010), PUID checked with kscePUIDtoGUID unless -1, then sds_dev_sd_op. cmd 7: format: sds_sd_write_mbr, then sds_slot_invalidate; cmd 8: sds_slot_invalidate only (devices 1/4, nothing open). Unknown cmd -> 0x80010030, bad device -> 0x80010016

name: sds_vfs_register
notes: heap "SceSdStorVfs" (0x2000) -> 0x8100871c; SceVfsInfo at 0x810086fc {ops 0x810063f4, name "sdstor_dev_fs" (len 14), type 0x10, default vops 0x81006440}; ksceVfsAddVfs, then ksceIoMount(1, ...) mounts sdstor0: (iofilemgr mount id 1); on failure the heap is deleted

name: sds_usbmass_cb_a
notes: entry of the callback table at 0x810064c8 given to USB mass storage: SceUsbMassForDriver_3C821E99() if DAT_81007014 is set, else 0

name: sds_usbmass_cb_b
notes: second callback: SceUsbMassForDriver_7833D935() if DAT_81007010 is set, else 0

name: sds_usbmass_intr
notes: interrupt handler for "SceUsbMass" (interrupt 0xF): SceUsbMassForDriver_F2BAB182()

name: sds_usbmass_intr_init
notes: ksceKernelRegisterIntrHandler(0xF, "SceUsbMass", 0, sds_usbmass_intr, 0, 0xD0, 0xF, opt {0x14, 2, 0x810064b4})

name: sds_card_insert_subintr
notes: card-insert sub-interrupt handler: sets bit 1 of the slot event flag (s+4)

name: sds_card_remove_subintr
notes: card-remove sub-interrupt handler: sets bit 0x10 of the slot event flag

name: sds_sysevent
prototype: int sds_sysevent(int resume, int ev, void *, void *opt)
notes: suspend/resume system event handler. ev 0x200 (phase 0): tells the slot threads of devices 1 and 2 (and 4 with model capability 0xB) to suspend (event bit 0x100) and waits for their acknowledgement. ev 0x400D (phase 0): disables the SD and memory card sub-interrupts and powers both slots off. ev 0x100000 (once, opt+5 guards it): tells the threads to resume (bit 0x1000) and waits; ev 0x400000 clears the guard

name: sds_read_mediaid
notes: for device 1 or 2 (r+0x24; others 0x80010013): sds_dev_check, sector 0 into a private buffer (0x81008720 / 0x81008920), must be a Sony MBR; the last partition entry with code 0x0D (mediaid) gives a start sector, whose first sector is read into the same buffer; none -> 0x80010002

name: sds_slot_mount_default
notes: when the slot device (s+0x24) becomes the default memory device: in internal-storage-only mode via sds_default_int_dev, mount ID 0xE00 (xmc0:); otherwise via sds_default_ext_dev, mount ID 0x800 (ux0:). It posts SceIofilemgrForDriver_39ABDB9E(id, 0x100) (media available) and, unless internal-only or slot flag bit 0 (+0x26) is set, ksceIoMount(id, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0). Not the default -> 0, nothing done

name: sds_slot_on_suspend
notes: disables the slot card sub-interrupts; if a card is present (+0x25 == 1) its CID is saved in s+0x14 (16 x 0xFA when the CID reads as zero); sds_dev_mark_removed; device 4 also calls SceSysconForDriver_F99BC858

name: sds_slot_unmount_memcard
notes: memory-device removal: if the slot is the default device, ksceIoUmount(0x800 or 0xE00, 1 = force). Then vfsRmdev("sdstor0:NNN") for every resolved slot 0..16, sds_dev_suspend_a, SceIofilemgrForDriver_39ABDB9E(id, 0x200) (media gone) when it was the default, and the default-device claim is released

name: sds_slot_on_resume
notes: restores the slot state and re-initialises the device (sds_dev_reinit_removable); device 4 also needs SceSysconForDriver_F99BC858 bit 0 clear. The CID is re-read and compared with the one saved at suspend: same card -> nothing; a different card -> the old one is unmounted (sds_slot_unmount_memcard), the slot reset and sds_slot_mount_default run; failure -> unmount and reset. Then SceIofilemgrForDriver_5B7E5AB8(0x800 / 0xD00 / 0xE00, 0) for the affected mount IDs and the sub-interrupts are re-enabled

name: sds_gc_unmount
notes: game-card removal: ksceIoUmount(0x900 gro0, 0xA00 grw0, 0x100 sd0:, force), vfsRmdev of all its slots, sds_dev_suspend_a, then 39ABDB9E(id, 0x200) for the three. So sd0: lives on the game-card slot (device 1)

name: sds_slot_on_remove
notes: card removed (only if +0x25 marks one present). Device 1: a game-card slot (F804F761 == 0) -> sds_gc_unmount, else the memory-card path; then sds_dev_shutdown. Device 2 or 4: unmount ux0:/xmc0: if default, rmdev all slots, suspend, notify 0x200, release the default, shutdown. Device 3 (USB): ksceIoUmount(0xF00 uma0:, force), rmdev, suspend, 39ABDB9E(0xF00, 0x200), shutdown. Clears the saved CID; +0x25 := 0 unless it is 2

name: sds_slot_thread
notes: SceSdstorIntr thread, one per removable slot (1..4; 4 only with model capability 0xB). With external storage the slot device is probed first (present -> state 1). The card insert/remove sub-interrupts are enabled, then the loop waits on the slot event flag for bits 0x1113, filtered by the mask for the current state (0x81006530). Bit 1 is a remove request: a game card for which sds_dev_media_op succeeds counts as still present, and an SD that fails a one-sector read counts as removed. Bit 0x100 is suspend: memory card and game card write 16 random bytes (ksceSblRngPseudoRandomNumber) to the first sector of their mediaid partition (mcd-/gcd-lp-act-mediaid) and remember them; SD and device 4 save their CID (sds_slot_on_suspend); state 2. Bit 0x1000 is resume: the stored media id or CID is compared with the card now present. A different or missing card is unmounted and the new one remounted (memory card: sds_slot_mount_default; game card: 39ABDB9E(id, 0x100) and ksceIoMount for gro0 0x900, grw0 0xA00, and sd0 0x100 only if neither game mount succeeded, read-only flag 0x1000 when write-protected except for grw0); sub-interrupts are re-enabled. Bit 0x10 is insert, in state 0: the device is re-initialised and its slot cleared. The memory card resets its mediaid sector and runs sds_slot_mount_default (ux0:/xmc0:); the game card resets mediaid and mounts gro0/grw0/sd0 as above; device 4 and an SD in slot 1 run sds_slot_mount_default; USB (device 3) is only brought up, uma0: is not mounted here. Bit 1 with a card present -> sds_slot_on_remove. Each handled bit is acknowledged on the OpSync event flag

name: sds_slot_init
notes: registers the "SceSdstor" sysevent handler (sds_sysevent). Clears the slot table (0x81008b20, 5 x 0x28) and both mediaid buffers. For slots 1..4 (4 only with model capability 0xB) it sets the insert/remove handlers and the sub-interrupt numbers (2 and 3 use sub-interrupts 0/1), and creates a "SceSdstorIntr" thread (priority 0x1C, stack 0x2000, attr 0x80000). It also creates the event flags "SceSdstorRequest" (requests) and "SceSdstorOpSync" (acknowledgements), disables both card sub-interrupts, registers "SceSdstorCardInsert"/"SceSdstorCardRemove" sub-interrupt handlers and starts the thread with its slot number
